terminology.name: Phase
terminology.definition: An outcome, milestone, delivery, governance, or material risk boundary; not an invocation, retry, provider, model, or conversation-turn counter.
terminology.authority: PHASE_CONTROL plus immutable boundary revision records

terminology.name: Task
terminology.definition: A stable governed unit of work inside a Phase; a persistent governed Task has exactly one Result Contract lineage.
terminology.authority: Result Contract lineage with a Phase binding

terminology.name: Round
terminology.definition: A Result Contract execution-entry budget unit committed when Task state enters EXECUTING from a non-EXECUTING state.

terminology.name: Attempt
terminology.definition: One explicitly authorized bounded try with its own identity, start, completion, result, evidence, and zero or more Invocations.

terminology.name: Invocation
terminology.definition: One tool, provider, process, or command invocation within an Attempt; it contains zero or more observed external requests.

terminology.name: Request Intent
terminology.definition: One logical, pre-authorized external side-effect intent reserved before dispatch; it is not proof that a physical request was sent.

terminology.name: Observed Request
terminology.definition: One physical external request for which direct evidence exists; unknown additional provider retries remain represented by incomplete observation.
terminology.authority: EXTERNAL_REQUEST_OBSERVED event plus Invocation dispatch summary

terminology.name: Authorization Envelope
terminology.definition: An immutable grant that binds an accepted contract revision and Phase boundary to allowed operations, scope, time, and incremental counted-unit limits.

terminology.name: Session Lease
terminology.definition: The unique active canonical-write ownership grant for one bounded Session, intersected with Phase, Result Contract, and user authorization.
terminology.authority: SESSION_CONTROL structured lease and workspace v4 binding

invariants.statement: A Phase is selected by outcome, milestone, delivery, governance, or material risk boundary; invocation, retry, provider, model, and conversation turn are not automatic Phase boundaries.
Attempt, Invocation, or queue-Task failure must not automatically promote a Result Contract or Phase to terminal BLOCKED or FAILED.
An accepted Phase boundary is an immutable revision; material change requires a hash-bound boundary amendment revision or Phase transition, and terminal Phase bodies remain unchanged.
Each governed persistent Task has exactly one Result Contract v2 lineage; Phase, Session, report, handoff, runtime, and lineage index surfaces store only bindings or rebuildable projections.

Contract revisions and typed events are immutable regular non-reparse workspace files; every event has one monotonically increasing sequence and binds the exact previous event hash except sequence one.
Corrections append CORRECTION_APPENDED events; they do not edit committed revisions or events. The latest index can be rebuilt only from the declared lineage and must match the Phase binding.

Task status transitions, Rounds, Attempts, Invocations, request intents, observed requests, authorization, and recovery observations are different event kinds with separate identifiers and cardinality.
Round retains the v1 execution-entry meaning and increments only when a committed ROUND_STARTED event moves a Task from non-EXECUTING to EXECUTING.

A valid authorization envelope binds one contract revision, Phase boundary revision, allowed operation/scope, validity interval, and incremental limits; it does not replace hard contract budgets or Session lease checks.
No ROUND_STARTED event may commit when max_authorized_rounds is exhausted, even if max_rounds and other hard budgets remain.

A logical request intent is reserved before dispatch; request observations separately record known physical requests, completeness, outcome, and charge state. Exit code alone does not prove CONFIRMED_NOT_SENT.

UNKNOWN dispatch, observation completeness, outcome, or charge state under a finite hard request/side-effect bound stops further execution until explicit reconciliation and authorization; MALTS makes no cross-system exactly-once claim.

A finite hard physical-request limit must not be accepted when the selected provider/tool can perform unbounded or unobservable internal retries; logical Request Intent reservation is not proof of a physical-request upper bound.
At most one Session is active. Its structured lease has one owner, scope, touch set, allowed operations, grant time, and optional expiry; only that valid owner commits canonical state while active.

A canonical mutation is accepted only after exact plan/input preconditions, a workspace lock and journal, deterministic staged outputs, ordered replacements, and a COMMITTED journal state; governed readers fail closed while the transaction is incomplete.
MALTS must not claim instantaneous multi-file visibility or automatic crash rollback; interrupted transactions require explicit, exact-journal-bound recovery.

Workspace v3 to v4 and Result Contract v1 to v2 are independent dry-run-first, exact-plan/input-hash-bound cold migrations; ordinary read, validate, recover, init, or lifecycle mutation never migrates silently.

Migration must not proceed with an active Session, running Attempt or Invocation, unresolved external side effect, or incomplete workspace or Artifact transaction, and must not fabricate legacy typed events.
Recording only a Plan Recheck trigger/result preserves the existing canonical recovery summary, next action, and evidence references unless the reviewed operation explicitly replaces recovery.

Fast Path may reduce record overhead only; it must not bypass authorization, Phase boundary, active plan, Session lease, Artifact ownership, external-side-effect, or structural and binding consistency gates.
